Compiler architecture

An original compiler, still on its bootstrap.

The compiler is a working language implementation, but PEACOCK is not self-hosting and does not yet emit native code or WebAssembly.

The real compilation pipeline

Source passes through the same stages used by the CLI and tests.

Implemented

Lex and parse

Token stream → AST with source spans and recoverable Python-bootstrap diagnostics.

Python authoritative

Semantic analysis

Name resolution, scopes, types, function calls, returns and capability checks annotate the AST.

Verified subset

IR and optimisation

Typed linear IR is verified before and after constant/branch folding and dead temporary elimination.

Python runtime

Bytecode and VM

The bytecode image is verified, fingerprinted and run by PEACOCK's custom stack VM.

Bootstrap and self-hosting

A PEACOCK-written component is not the same thing as a self-hosting compiler.

Parity-tested

Tokenizer and parser

PEACOCK source tokenizes and parses the core grammar; parser parity uses structural AST digests across 18 .pac files.

Shadow mode · 74 checks

Semantic kernel

selfhost/type_model.pac probes relations, operators, lists/indexing, local scopes, names, declarations, assignments, structs, fields, properties, methods, signatures, calls, conditions and returns.

Stage 4 · 15 checks

IR & bytecode kernel

selfhost/ir_model.pac models linear PIR register def-before-use invariants, slot ranges, label uniqueness, try/catch balance, constant folding and jump targets.

Still Python

Production semantics

The Python SemanticAnalyzer, IRBuilder and VM remain the authoritative production pipeline until full fixed-point parity passes.
